headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets while marker is unverified and may ingest shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker has no filesystem read/write or MCP, so it cannot directly ingest nullclaw output by default. But nullclaw can read/write workspace files and uses browser/web/file channels, so if marker’s documents are placed in a shared workspace, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace directory
IF marker parses untrusted document text as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable shared file handoff
Add a provenance header to exchanged documents
Review any document containing imperative text before passing it onward

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, while marker is a document-processing agent with no declared isolation or redaction controls. Because nullclaw can read files and broad workspace state, any sensitive document processed by marker can be exposed through shared files or logs. The pair creates a realistic exfiltration path in default workspace-sharing setups.
conditions: IF marker processes documents containing secrets or regulated data
IF nullclaw is granted access to the same workspace or logs
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the shared workspace
Restrict nullclaw to a separate directory
Turn off or minimize audit logging for sensitive runs
Use redacted copies for document processing
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker is documented as unable to write or modify state, while nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and use broad network and subprocess capabilities. If both are pointed at the same directory or repo, nullclaw can overwrite marker outputs or race on shared files without coordination. The asymmetry makes conflicts likely and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem path or git repository
IF nullclaw is allowed to write while marker is used as a producer or reviewer
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Disable git writes for nullclaw during shared runs
Serialize access with a lock file
Use read-only mounts for marker inputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can generate extracted document content, and nullclaw has action-taking surfaces such as webhooks, APIs, scheduling, and browser/tool use. If nullclaw consumes marker output without verification, extraction errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair is not automatically dangerous, but the default workflow can amplify mistakes.
conditions: IF marker output is forwarded directly into nullclaw workflows
IF nullclaw acts on extracted text without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on marker output
Limit nullclaw to read-only dry runs
Log and diff extracted fields before action
requires-engineering: add confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and agent-card metadata, while marker is a document-processing agent with no stated retention or residency controls. If regulated documents are processed by marker and then stored or logged by nullclaw, retention and residency mismatches can occur. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined handling path.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed through the pair
IF nullclaw retains logs or workspace files longer than the source policy allows
mitigations: Minimize retained logs
Use region-appropriate storage
Delete processed artifacts promptly
Document data-handling responsibilities
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
